metadata.color_semantics: Claude fidelity skin throughout. Terracotta marks exactly one thing per beat: the REVIEW move (B02), the legibility catch (B03), the round-2 score (B04), the ambiguous count (B05), the patterns row (B06), the method row (B07). Everything else is warm ink on cream.
metadata.note: Progress update on the week of 2026-11-09 — the second of the week's two videos. Toolkit-only patterns (ClaudeComposerAsk, ReelExecSummary, ReelFramework, BlipLadder, ClaudeVerdictArtifact, ClaudeTitleOutro). 16:9 only — progress updates ship in landscape; the explainer carries the 9:16 cut. Every figure comes from this week's explainer build (PROOF-REVIEW.md, measured audio, clip check, GATE V) or the sources it cites.

props.title: Week 11 Progress: Inkling
thesis: A two-minute Inkling teardown built on a reusable four-step audit,
self-reviewed with a teaching rubric before any frame was rendered.

roadmap.label: Caught
roadmap.body: Four claims voiced before they were on screen.

roadmap.label: Corrected
roadmap.body: Two draft facts the sources didn't support as written.

roadmap.label: Open
roadmap.body: A parameter count the config can't settle.

beats.narration: Four moves this week. Read the config, the weight map, the model card and the announcement. Re-cut the draft onto six proven patterns. Review it with the rubric. Then narrate, render twice at 4K, and check the frames. Move three is the new one.
beats.narration_text: Four moves this week. Read the config, the weight map, the model card and the announcement. Re-cut the draft onto six proven patterns. Review it with the rubric. Then narrate, render twice at 4K, and check the frames. Move three is the new one.

props.heading: How the week went

moves.label: READ
moves.detail: config.json, the weight map, the model card, the announcement.

moves.label: AUTHOR
moves.detail: A draft for 8 unbuilt scenes → 12 beats on 6 proven patterns.

moves.label: REVIEW
moves.detail: PROOF self-review on the beat sheet, before any audio.

moves.label: BUILD
moves.detail: Narration 2:07.5, 4K twice, clip lengths, frames in both cuts.

props.keepNote: Move 3 is new: the rubric graded the sheet while every fix was still a cheap edit.
props.source: This week’s build — PROOF-REVIEW.md · clip check · GATE V reports

beats.narration: What the review caught. The worked example's arithmetic was spoken at the start of its beat but only appeared at eighty percent. Three claims were voiced and never shown. And step four named no test that could break anything.
beats.narration_text: What the review caught. The worked example's arithmetic was spoken at the start of its beat but only appeared at eighty percent. Three claims were voiced and never shown. And step four named no test that could break anything.

props.heading: What the review caught

moves.label: LEGIBILITY
moves.detail: B05 arithmetic voiced at ~7% of the beat, on screen at 80%.

moves.label: UNSHOWN
moves.detail: B00's 975B, B06's 1.9 TB and B09's open data were voiced only.

moves.label: NO TEST
moves.detail: Step 4 listed caveats but named no result that would break a claim.

moves.label: FIXES
moves.detail: Six edits to the sheet: rows that appear as they're spoken.

props.keepNote: Every catch was found from the sheet and the reveal timings — before a frame existed.

beats.narration: The score. The rubric's own ship bar is eight out of twelve. I set ten for these weeks. The first draft scored ten, but failed the production gate. After six edits: twelve, and the gate passed. And a ten that fails the gate still doesn't ship.

props.heading: Teaching score, out of 12
props.exception: A 10 that fails the gate still doesn't ship: the evidence has to be readable when it's claimed.

beats.narration: What the sources corrected. The draft said a benchmark was zeroed out; the announcement says some contaminated solutions were. The dense layers are now checked in the weight map. And the parameter count stayed ambiguous. A researched draft is still a draft.
beats.narration_text: What the sources corrected. The draft said a benchmark was zeroed out; the announcement says some contaminated solutions were. The dense layers are now checked in the weight map. And the parameter count stayed ambiguous. A researched draft is still a draft.

props.heading: What the sources corrected

moves.label: LEAKAGE
moves.detail: Not a benchmark zeroed: some contaminated solutions scored 0.

moves.label: DENSE
moves.detail: Layers 1–2 dense: confirmed in the weight map, not inferred.

moves.label: COUNT
moves.detail: 975B stated; 1.905 TB ÷ 2 bytes ≈ 952B — kept as ambiguous.

props.keepNote: A researched draft is still a draft. The receipts get the last word.
props.source: Thinking Machines, Introducing Inkling (Jul 15, 2026) · model.safetensors.index.json · model card

beats.narration: What shipped: two 4K masters with identical audio, twelve beats, six toolkit patterns, and no new scene code. Both cuts passed the frame gate, but my own frame check caught two labels running into their text.

props.heading: Week 11 — shipped

moves.label: BEATS
moves.detail: 12 beats; every number carries its source in frame.

moves.label: PATTERNS
moves.detail: 6 toolkit patterns, all with 9:16 twins — 0 new scene code.

moves.label: QC
moves.detail: GATE V clean in both cuts; frame review caught 2 overlapping labels → 2 beats re-rendered.

props.keepNote: The draft asked for eight new scenes. The review showed the teaching never needed them.
props.source: This week’s build — clip check and GATE V reports, both orientations

beats.narration: What carries over. Sparse compute isn't sparse memory. Grading the sheet against the reveal timings catches problems while they're cheap. And look at the frames yourself: the automated gate passed two labels that overlapped their text. Still open: nine seventy-five billion, or nine fifty-two?

props.heading: Week 11 — learned, open, next

moves.label: LEARNED
moves.detail: Sparse compute isn't sparse memory: 41B active, 1.9 TB resident.

moves.label: METHOD
moves.detail: Grade the sheet against the reveal timings before rendering.

moves.label: FRAMES
moves.detail: GATE V passed two labels that overlap their text. Look at the frames.

moves.label: OPEN
moves.detail: 975B vs ≈ 952B: mixed precision or counting? Not stated.

props.keepNote: The method row is the keeper: it moves quality checks before the expensive step.
